answer: Proposed ocean-survey payouts bind one key to one certified glider hull for 30 days. A shore beacon orders each hull to wander through a random patrol track; independent hydrophones triangulate signed pings concurrently. Validators check one key per serial. A farm rents gliders and shares software, but k keys still need k hulls at once; one hull cannot occupy two tracks. If pings are missing, that key earns zero; a forged signed path burns its separate deposit exceeding capped 30-day pay. Trusted certifiers and hydrophones must enforce this; MinePoA does not.
